fields.meta_title: Wedding RSVP Form Builder With Meal Choices | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a wedding RSVP form where guests find their household, pick a meal, and get reminders, and every reply saves to a guest list you own.
fields.h1: Build a Wedding RSVP Form for Every Household
fields.hero_description: Build a wedding RSVP site that finds each guest's invitation and takes meal choices, with every reply in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything Between the Invite and the Headcount
fields.features_subheading: Describe how your invitations work. Emergent builds the site guests reply on, the rules behind it, and the guest list it fills.
fields.feature_1:
Plus-ones only where you offer them

Mark which invitations include a guest. Those households see a field for the extra name, and the rest see only the people you invited. A plus-one saves to the list like any guest.
fields.feature_2:
Questions past yes or no

Ask for a song request, a hotel booking, or a shuttle seat. Each answer saves as its own column beside the guest's name, ready to filter when the planner asks who rides the bus.
fields.feature_3:
A headcount that moves with each reply

Open the dashboard to see who is attending, who declined, and who is still waiting. Totals change the moment a guest submits, and the venue gets the number on the screen.
fields.feature_4:
Replies guests can change until the date

Let guests reopen their RSVP from the same link until the reply date. A change replaces the old answer and logs when it happened. After the date, the page shows your contact details.
fields.feature_5:
The site at a domain you choose

Publish the RSVP page at your own wedding domain instead of a platform address. Custom domains are included with Emergent and use credits. Guests type the address on the card.
fields.feature_6:
The code, in your own GitHub repository

Export the full RSVP site to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The guest list and every saved reply move with it, and a friend who writes code can host it after the wedding.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Weddings, Four Ways Guests Reply
fields.tab_content_1:
Two yes and one no from the Okafor household

Leila and Owen print one link on every invitation. Nadia Okafor types her last name and sees the 3 guests her invitation names. She marks herself and Chidi attending and Ada declined. Her household has no plus-one, and the page offers no extra-guest field. The couple's guest list saves 2 attending and 1 declined.
fields.tab_content_2:
The caterer gets 142 plates counted by guest name

Every attending guest picks an entree under their own name, with a box for allergies. When replies close 3 weeks before the wedding, Larkspur Catering gets the count: 61 short rib, 48 salmon, and 33 risotto, which makes 142 plates. The 7 allergy notes travel with it, each one beside the guest who wrote it.
fields.tab_content_3:
With 10 days to go, 23 households get a reminder

Leila and Owen invited 96 households, and 73 have replied with 10 days left before the reply date. Each of the other 23 gets an email reminder with its own RSVP link. Within 3 days, 14 of them answer. Owen gets the last 9 as a call list with a phone number for each.
fields.tab_content_4:
For cousin Lucia, two events; for Theo, all three

Marisol and Ben invite 150 guests to the ceremony and the Sunday brunch, and 40 of them to the welcome dinner. Each guest's page lists only their events. Lucia Ferro, a cousin, sees two. Theo Grant, a groomsman, sees all three. Replies save per event, and the restaurant gets a list of 40 names.

fields.howto_title: How to Put Your Wedding RSVP Online
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to put your wedding RSVP online with meal choices and reminders, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose how guests find their names
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask the meal question per guest
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the reply date and reminders
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put every invited household in one sheet, with the names exactly as the envelope carries them and whether the invitation includes a plus-one. Add an email address or phone number for each household. The RSVP page looks guests up in this table.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick a last-name search or a short code printed on the card. A search suits older relatives; a code keeps two households named Garcia apart. Either way, show the matched names before anyone answers, and let guests try again if the match is wrong.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask every attending guest to pick a dish, one choice per person, plus a box for allergies. Use the caterer's dish names, and the count you send will match the menu card. Give children's meals their own option if the caterer prices them differently.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the date replies close and when a household that has not answered gets a reminder, such as 10 days before. Decide who hears about the households still silent after that, and whether the note arrives by email or in Slack.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the lookup, the plus-one rule, the meal question, and the reminder schedule into one prompt. Emergent builds the site and the guest table from it. Change anything later by asking for it in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Print the address on the card
fields.howto_step_6_des: Print the site address or a QR code that opens it on the invitation, with the reply date beside it. Guests who prefer paper can still mail a card back. Enter those replies on the same list, and the headcount stays whole.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the invitations go out, reply as a household with a plus-one, one without, and one that declines. Check that the meal count and the dashboard show what you expect, then delete the test replies.

faq_plan.q: What is the best website to RSVP for a wedding?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best website to RSVP for a wedding?

prov.original: What is the best website to RSVP for a wedding?

faq_plan.a: The best website is the one the couple printed on your invitation: their wedding RSVP page is where your reply reaches the guest list. If you are the couple and still choosing, look for a lookup that shows each household only its invited guests, a meal question per person, and a way to export every reply.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a wedding RSVP online?
faq_plan.ref: how to make wedding rsvp online
faq_plan.a: Describe the invitation to Emergent's AI form builder: who each household includes and which invitations carry a plus-one. Add the meal options and the reply date. It builds the RSVP site and the guest table behind it. Publish the site and print its address on the card.

faq_plan.q: How to do an online RSVP for a wedding?
faq_plan.ref: How to do an online RSVP for a wedding?

prov.original: How to do an online RSVP for a wedding?

faq_plan.a: Open the link or QR code on the invitation and find your name. Mark each person the invitation names as attending or not, and pick a meal if the couple asks. Submit before the reply date. Couples who build their RSVP page on Emergent keep every reply in a database they own.

faq_plan.q: How far in advance should you send out RSVP for a wedding?
faq_plan.ref: How far in advance should you send out RSVP for a wedding?

prov.original: How far in advance should you send out RSVP for a wedding?

faq_plan.a: Send the invitation with its RSVP card or link 6 to 8 weeks before the wedding, which is Zola's advice for official invitations. Zola puts the RSVP deadline two to three weeks before the wedding. Treat that date like the closing date on a job application form: print it beside the link, and leave a few days after it to call anyone who has not answered.

faq_plan.q: Where can I get free digital wedding invitations with RSVP?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I get free digital wedding invitations with RSVP?

prov.original: Where can I get free digital wedding invitations with RSVP?

faq_plan.a: Joy and Greetings Island are two places to start. Joy pairs free online RSVP with its wedding website, and Greetings Island has online RSVP templates that are free to customize and can be sent electronically. Before you choose, send a test invitation to yourself and check what a guest sees when they reply.

faq_plan.q: How do I fill out a wedding RSVP card?
faq_plan.ref: how do i fill out a wedding rsvp card
faq_plan.a: Write your names on the line that starts with M; Zola says that line is for guests' names with their titles, such as Mr. or Ms. Then check accept or decline and write the number attending. If the card lists entrees, Zola's advice is to put each guest's initials next to their meal. Mail it back before the reply date.

faq_plan.q: What should a wedding RSVP form include?
faq_plan.ref: what to include on wedding rsvp form
faq_plan.a: Include the names the invitation covers, an accept or decline for each person, a meal choice per attending guest, and the reply date. Add a plus-one field only on invitations that offer one, plus a box for allergies. Ask only what you will act on; the same rule keeps an interest form to a few questions.

faq_plan.q: How do I turn wedding RSVP replies into a seating chart?
faq_plan.ref: how to do an online wedding rsvp card
faq_plan.a: Start from the attending guests, sorted by household, and give each family one table to begin with. Add a table-number column to the guest list and fill it in as the plan settles. Emergent can add a seating view to the RSVP site with one more prompt, reading the replies already saved.

faq_plan.q: How do I add a late guest to a wedding RSVP list?
faq_plan.ref: how to complete a wedding rsvp card
faq_plan.a: Add the household as a new row on the guest list, with its names, its plus-one setting, and a way to reach it. It can find its invitation on the RSVP page as soon as the row is saved. Give it a reply date that still leaves time to update the caterer's count.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect mailing addresses on a wedding RSVP form?
faq_plan.ref: how to complete wedding rsvp form
faq_plan.a: Add one mailing address field per household, and the thank-you cards go to the address the guests typed themselves. Ask for it after the attendance question, and only once per invitation. The form Emergent builds saves it on the household's row, the way it keeps answers on any form tied to named people, such as an advance directive form.

plan.angle: The top 10 is wedding platforms (The Knot guest list, Zola and Joy wedding websites, RSVPify), paper RSVP cards (Minted, The Knot paper, Greetings Island) and etiquette posts on wording and how to reply. They either rent the couple a fixed RSVP page or sell a card. This page answers the guest and etiquette questions directly (timing, filling in the card, where to RSVP free) and shows what a couple gets by building their own wedding RSVP site: guests find their household and answer only for the people invited, each guest picks a meal that becomes the caterer's count, quiet households get reminders before the reply date, and a weekend with several events invites each guest to only their events, with every reply in a database the couple owns.
